correctness.rationale: Strict sine concavity gives the unique global equilateral maximum T=2 sqrt(3). Compact localization and the maximum-gap cusp yield |delta|=O(t). The exact wedge identity T=4 sin(pi/3-r/4) cos(3ru/4), jacobian 3r/2, and uniform implicit radial expansion imply CDF=9t^2/pi^2-18 sqrt(3)t^3/pi^2+O(t^4). Normalized wedge densities converge in L1 to a product of Uniform(3 labels), Beta(2,1), and Uniform[-1,1], proving total variation. The perimeter limit follows by quadratic Taylor expansion. Exact small-threshold quadratures, independent simplex-grid integration and iid-circle simulation from the included path verify numerical implications, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A Euclidean MST is a canonical shortest connection network. The nonsmooth deletion of the largest chord produces an exact quadratic rare-event probability instead of the smooth perimeter linear law; the explicit second term and independent marked shape reveal which spanning topology dominates and how angular and perimeter fluctuations separate into linear versus quadratic scales. These are motivated geometric stability and rare-network shape results, not a renamed perimeter calculation.
